name: Maniv
identity_check: Confirmed as Maniv (maniv.com), also styled Maniv Mobility: the early-stage VC Michael Granoff founded in Tel Aviv in 2015, with offices at Menachem Begin 144, Tel Aviv and in New York. The site's LinkedIn link (company/maniv-mobilityvc) redirects to the 'Maniv' company page (HQ Tel Aviv). TechCrunch (2019, 2024) and Maniv's 2024 Business Wire release describe the same firm and partners; its fund vehicles on SEC EDGAR are named Maniv Mobility (A, II, III, Special Opportunities). Legal entity named in one round report: Maniv Mobility Management Ltd. An independent VC, not a corporate venture arm of its automotive LPs.

thesis_text.value: Early-stage firm backing startups that rebuild the physical economy in four areas: making (manufacturing, materials, new production models), moving (autonomy, new vehicle formats, smarter logistics), powering (grid modernisation driven by AI compute, EVs and reindustrialisation) and computing (new silicon, memory and processors). It grew out of a mobility-only focus on moving people and goods.

requires_us_entity: no stated policy. Maniv has backed non-US companies (Bengaluru-based Fresh Bus, Stockholm-based Engrate, Israeli NeoLogic, Brazilian Vammo), but their holding structures are unknown.

SEC EDGAR: the full-text search index answered and gives fund legal names and Form D dates (Maniv Mobility A, LP 2016-07-20 Westwood NJ; Maniv Mobility II, L.P. 2018-06-29 and D/A 2019-07-09 Tel Aviv; Maniv Mobility III, L.P. 2022-06-03 New York; Special Opportunities, L.P. Series 1-12, 2021-08-30 to 2026-07-13). The Form D documents on sec.gov/Archives refused the declared User-Agent (403), so offering sizes were not read. Mapping 'Maniv Mobility A, LP' to the $44M first fund is an inference from its 2016 filing date.
Special Opportunities Series 1-12 look like deal-by-deal vehicles; sizes, targets and close dates unknown. No fourth flagship fund found as of Oct 2026 (Fund III announced Apr 2024).
Fund close dates are announcement dates; Fund I close date not published.
New York address differs between pages: 1900 Broadway (homepage) vs 135 West 50th Street (contact page).

Rounds not recorded: Robot Toolworx seed (Mar 2026, ~$5.6M per Caplight search hint; no press or firm page found); Mundimoto $21M (elEconomista 403); Anaphite EUR 1.6M Dec 2025 (EU-Startups 403); RightHand Robotics $66M 2022 (Forbes 403); Terraline $7M seed 2022 (Business Wire 403); Hailo $120M Series C extension (Calcalist page does not name Maniv). A search hint (f4.fund, not readable) says Maniv led Vammo's $45M, contradicting Construct's post (Ecosystem Integrity Fund led).

Partner focus_sectors: maniv.com/team gives titles only (bio for Granoff only). Jaret, Dardashti and Wieseneck focus come from VC Sheet bios (database): fleets, energy, logistics, mobility. Hillel Zand's from his MobilityMonday posts on Engrate and Anaphite. No team LinkedIn links on maniv.com. Venture Advisor Venki Padmanabhan and advisory board (e.g. Neil Ackerman, J&J supply chain; Michael Newcity, ex-ArcBest) not recorded as partners.
Founded year not stated on the round pages for Harbinger, Vammo, Anaphite, Fresh Bus, Circular, Celadyne and Seurat; Seurat HQ is the release dateline (Wilmington, Mass.).
